reproduction_target: Training and application of REPRESS, a sequence-to-function deep-learning model (TensorFlow) that predicts cell-type-specific miRNA binding and mRNA (degradome) degradation from RNA sequence. Computational reproduction spans: (a) upstream sequencing-data processing pipelines for curated public AGO2-CLIP/PAR-CLIP/HITS-CLIP/eCLIP data (fastp, bowtie/bowtie2, picard, PARalyzer, CLIPper) and for study-generated miR-eCLIP / Degradome-Seq / Small-RNA-Seq (umi-tools, Cutadapt, STAR, HISAT2, featureCounts, miRBase); (b) transcript annotation/curation (GenomeKit RefSeq + APPRIS); (c) REPRESS architecture, 4-fold cross-validated ensemble training, evaluation/benchmarking vs TargetScan and biochemical models; (d) interpretation and downstream analyses (in-silico mutagenesis, smoothgrad attribution, ClinVar 3'UTR VUS scoring, ASO/MPRA/therapeutic-design analyses). Wet-lab data generation (cell culture; miR-eCLIP, Degradome-Seq, Small-RNA-Seq library prep, performed by EclipseBio) is out of computational-reproduction scope and counted in W.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool (or per coherent tool group) from the Methods subsections 'Data generation and processing', 'Model Architecture', 'Model training and evaluation', and the interpretation/analysis subsections. Upstream per-protocol pipelines are grouped: PAR-CLIP (C1-C3), HITS-CLIP/eCLIP (C4-C5). Study-generated miR-eCLIP (umi-tools+Cutadapt+bowtie+STAR+CLIPper), Degradome-Seq (fastp+HISAT2), and Small-RNA-Seq (cutadapt+STAR+featureCounts) are each folded into one step (C6/C7/C8). The REPRESS package (github.com/deepgenomics/repress) contains the model + downstream analysis code (C9-C13); the upstream sequencing pipelines are described in prose with command-line args but are not evidently shipped as scripts in the repo. Version axis capped at 1 at stage1 per rubric; the repo's environment.yml is a CLAIM only (not read/executed at stage1).

steps.label: fastp read trimming for curated PAR-CLIP data (--adapter_sequence XXX -w 16 --trim_poly_x --cut_tail 30) [ref 82]
Genome alignment of PAR-CLIP reads with bowtie (-v 2 -m 1 --best --strata) [ref 83]
Peak calling on PAR-CLIP alignments with PARalyzer [ref 84]
HITS-CLIP/eCLIP trimming (fastp) + alignment with bowtie2 (-D 20 -R 3 -N 0 -L 20 -i S,1,0.50 -k 4 -p 32) + picard de-duplication [refs 85, picard]
Peak calling on HITS-CLIP/eCLIP alignments with CLIPper [ref 86]

Study-generated miR-eCLIP processing (EclipseBio): umi-tools UMI extraction, Cutadapt adapter trim, bowtie reverse-map to miRBase mature miRNAs, STAR genome alignment, CLIPper peak calling [refs 87-90]
Study-generated Degradome-Seq processing: fastp trim (--adapter_sequence XXX --length_required 20) + HISAT2 splice-aware alignment; read coverage used directly as training label [ref 91]
Study-generated Small-RNA-Seq processing: cutadapt (-m 15) + STAR (EndToEnd, extensive quant params) + featureCounts (-M -O -s 1 --minOverlap 3), CPM per miRNA averaged over replicates [refs 90, 92]
Transcript annotation/curation for training set: GenomeKit RefSeq v109 (human) / m38.v106 (mouse), APPRIS principal-transcript selection, protein-coding only, 3 kb windows + 6.25 kb context [ref 93]

REPRESS architecture (16 dilated-conv residual blocks) + training: 4-fold chromosome-split CV ensemble, BCE loss for miRNA head + Poisson loss for degradome head, species-specific gradient routing (TensorFlow 2.11)

Model evaluation and benchmarking: window-based average pooling + chunked metrics; comparison vs TargetScan, biochemical model, and other architectures across binding/degradation/transfection/knockout tasks
Sequence-attribution interpretation of REPRESS: in-silico mutagenesis (ISM), smoothgrad, complementarity/degradation maps

Downstream variant/therapeutic analyses: ClinVar 3'UTR VUS scoring, curated miRNA-blocking ASO prediction, PON1 SBO screening, synthetic-mRNA design; validation vs experimentally-validated sites (HEAP GSE139344) and transfection/knockout GEO datasets

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Under an inference-inclusive reading, the 5 model/annotation/analysis steps (C9-C13) are RI-capped: code is in a populated public repo (github.com/deepgenomics/repress) with an environment.yml carrying partial exact pins (tensorflow=2.11.*, genomekit=5.1.0) plus floating deps (python>=3.8, pandas>=2.0, numpy>=1.21,<1.25) and no lockfile/container — so version cannot exceed exact_pins_partial. The 5 upstream curated-CLIP steps (C1-C5) cap at NI: tool versions absent and pipeline scripts not evidently in the repo, though public GEO fastq exists. The 3 study-generated-data steps (C6-C8) are X: the newly generated miR-eCLIP / Degradome-Seq / Small-RNA-Seq raw data have no deposited accession and no data-availability statement, so their processing (and the labels they produce for training) cannot be reconstructed. This paper is a legitimate stage-2 candidate for C9-C13 via the repo, but full end-to-end reproduction is bounded by the undeposited generated data.
headline.coverage: 13 computational steps assessed from Methods prose; 4 wet-lab data-generation steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. Code available at github.com/deepgenomics/repress (live, HTTP 200). Public GEO accessions cited for curated/validation data (GSE60426, GSE97060, GSE123311, GSE127211, GSE139344, GSE197363); no accession for study-generated data.

gaps.where: Study-generated miR-eCLIP / Degradome-Seq / Small-RNA-Seq raw data (C6-C8)
gaps.missing: No deposited accession (GEO/SRA/ENA) and no data-availability statement for the sequencing data generated for this study by EclipseBio. These data provide a substantial fraction of the training labels, so both upstream processing and full model retraining cannot be reproduced from raw inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the generated miR-eCLIP, Degradome-Seq, and Small-RNA-Seq raw/processed data under a public accession and add an explicit data-availability statement mapping each cell line/tissue to its accession.

gaps.where: Software environment for the REPRESS repo (C9-C13) and all upstream pipelines (C1-C8)
gaps.missing: The repo ships a conda environment.yml with only partial exact pins (tensorflow=2.11.*, tensorflow-estimator=2.11.*, genomekit=5.1.0) mixed with floating/unpinned deps (python>=3.8, pandas>=2.0, numpy>=1.21,<1.25, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn) and no conda-lock/pip lockfile or container/digest. Upstream CLIP/seq tools (fastp, bowtie, bowtie2, picard, PARalyzer, CLIPper, umi-tools, Cutadapt, STAR, HISAT2, featureCounts) carry no version anywhere.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a fully resolved lock (conda-lock/pixi.lock) or a container digest for both the model environment and the upstream pipeline tools, recording exact versions of every named tool.

gaps.missing: The per-protocol pipelines are described as command-line invocations with arguments in prose, but the corresponding scripts/workflow do not appear to be shipped in the REPRESS repo (which contains the model + downstream analysis). No orchestration (Snakemake/Nextflow/shell) is provided to re-run trimming->alignment->peak-calling.
gaps.how_to_close: Add the upstream processing scripts/workflow (with tool versions and per-dataset config) to the repository or a companion pipeline repo.

gaps.missing: PARalyzer and CLIPper parameters are not specified; miR-eCLIP reverse-mapping and ISM/downstream-analysis hyperparameters are only partially stated in prose.
gaps.how_to_close: State exact peak-caller settings and record analysis hyperparameters/config in the repo.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: cell culture; miR-eCLIP, Degradome-Seq, and Small-RNA-Seq library preparation (EclipseBio)
gaps.missing: Wet-lab data-generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the computational pipeline and model.
